{"self_assessment": "Impact: I built the bottom line of the fish from the belly's low point through the tail crossing out to the tail tip, which is the stretch where the two outlines meet and the picture is most likely to break. I joined it onto Omar's last domino so the outline stayed one connected run. Tracing the start by eye, about 121 of the 124 standing dominoes were connected, and the result reads clearly as a fish.

Execution: I laid the tail section in several short builds, extending from the end of the line, then inspected the crossing and the bunched stretch just before it. I checked connectivity before the push and confirmed the chain carried through nearly everything. After that I kept my hands off the table so we avoided bumps in the final minutes.

Collaboration: I split the bottom line with Omar and agreed a clear handoff point, so we did not duplicate work. I said openly what I was taking and asked Omar to shout if he was already on it, which kept us coordinated. I accepted Omar's call to leave one domino alone and backed Sofia's plan to leave the crossing untouched.

Leadership: I took ownership of the hardest section, the tail crossing, and set out the handoff plan for it. I kept the table informed about what I was doing and when I was stepping back, and I helped us agree to stop touching the build so the picture was safe for the push.

Overall, I believe my part was a significant piece of the finished fish, mainly the tail join and its check, though the table's result was a team effort built on Sofia's sketch and the other lines.", "my_share_percent": 30}
